title: STITCHLINE — Home sewing machine stitch settings touchscreen, 6 deliverables

config.text:
# STITCHLINE — supplied prototype behaviour

## Scope and hardware

- Product: STITCHLINE home sewing machine touchscreen prototype
- Interface language: English
- Screen: landscape, 1024 × 600 logical pixels
- Physical controls: one Start/Pause button; one separate power switch
- Needle movement initiation: physical Start/Pause button exclusively
- Housing: existing enclosure; commission scope limited to the touchscreen interface
- Stitch preview: a diagram of the selected stitch path

## Three stitch records

- Length and width unit: millimetres (mm)
- Speed quantity: limit in stitches per minute (spm)
- Allowed speed limits for every stitch: 300, 450, 600 spm
- Range endpoints: inclusive
- Value progression: stated step from the minimum

| ID | Name | Preview identity | Length min / max / step | Width min / max / step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | Straight | Aligned punctures joined along one straight path | 0.5 / 4.0 / 0.5 mm | fixed 0.0 mm; not editable |
| S02 | Zigzag | Punctures alternate left/right along a repeating zigzag path | 0.5 / 3.0 / 0.5 mm | 1.0 / 6.0 / 0.5 mm |
| S03 | Long straight | Aligned punctures along a straight path, spacing at its default length visibly longer than S01 at its default length | 4.0 / 5.0 / 0.5 mm | fixed 0.0 mm; not editable |

## Draft defaults when changing from another stitch

| ID | Length | Width | Speed limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | 2.5 mm | 0.0 mm | 450 spm |
| S02 | 1.5 mm | 5.0 mm | 450 spm |
| S03 | 4.5 mm | 0.0 mm | 300 spm |

- Preview scale options: one common illustrative scale, or the line "Diagram — not to scale"
- Preview identity distinction: straight versus zigzag

## Draft, applied and motion rules

- Applied configuration: the last acknowledged complete tuple of stitch ID, length, width and speed limit
- Draft: a separate proposed tuple
- Catalogue selection, parameter change or preview change: applied tuple and motion unchanged
- Dirty state: a draft differing from the applied tuple, wherever that draft appears
- Discard: restoration of the complete applied tuple
- Apply submission: the complete draft
- Apply availability: machine Standby or Paused; needle-up sensor true; no active alert; every value within the selected stitch's ranges and increments
- Apply unavailable state: disabled action with the specific failing condition stated
- Acknowledged Apply outcome: complete new tuple applied; dirty marker cleared; existing Standby or Paused motion state retained
- Physical Start/Pause start or resume conditions: no alert and no unapplied draft
- Physical Start/Pause during Running: Pause request
- Physical Start/Pause during an alert: movement start inhibited
- Power switch: physical control only
- Running screen: viewing and navigation available; setting edits and Apply unavailable
- Pending edits while Paused: Apply or Discard resolution before physical resume becomes available

## Thread alert

- ID: T01
- Message: "Upper thread not detected"
- Trigger outcome: controller stops movement; motion marked Inhibited; last applied tuple preserved
- Acknowledge while the sensor reports missing thread: disabled
- Acknowledge once the controller reports clear: available
- Acknowledge outcome: Paused with the same applied tuple; motion stopped
- Hardware handling: machine's own printed instructions

## Six independent required snapshots

- A–D: one possible selection-to-running sequence
- E and F: separate later examples branching from D
- F draft relationship: none of E's draft carried into F

| Snapshot | Machine / needle-up / alert | Applied tuple: ID; length mm; width mm; limit spm | Draft | Recorded context |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Standby / true / none | S01; 2.5; 0.0; 450 | none | Catalogue browsing; S01 is the applied selection; all three records available |
| B | Standby / true / none | S01; 2.5; 0.0; 450 | S02; 1.5; 5.0; 450 | Editing S02; preview is a draft; opening review and discarding available |
| C | Standby / true / none | S01; 2.5; 0.0; 450 | S02; 1.5; 5.0; 450 | Pre-Apply review; no acknowledgement yet; Apply/Back/Discard available |
| D | Running / false / none | S02; 1.5; 5.0; 450 | none | New tuple acknowledged before a separate physical Start; 126 stitches recorded in current run |
| E | Paused / true / none | S02; 1.5; 5.0; 450 | S02; 2.0; 4.5; 300 | Proposed changes pending; run count remains 126; Apply/Discard available, resume blocked |
| F | Inhibited / false / T01 active | S02; 1.5; 5.0; 450 | none | Separate thread-alert branch; controller stopped at 139 recorded stitches; sensor still reports missing thread |

## Display conventions

- Recorded counts: stitches recorded in the current run
- Speed figures: limits rather than measured instantaneous rates
- Labels and microcopy: abbreviations allowed with meaning, ID, stitch name, number and unit retained exactly
- Product name placement: STITCHLINE on A and C
- B, D, E and F headings: compact stitch and state headings allowed
- Action wording: Review, Apply, Back, Discard, Acknowledge
- Default enabled component example: Review on B
- Pressed component example: Apply on C before release; applied tuple remains S01; controller acknowledgement pending
- Disabled component examples: editing and Apply on D; Acknowledge on F
- Error component example: T01 alert on F
- Body text contrast: at least 4.5:1
- Large text and icon contrast: at least 3:1
- State communication: words plus visual treatment

# STITCHLINE — delivery catalog

This table lists every commissioned deliverable with its tier, file format and stage. What each deliverable must contain is stated in the commission letter.

| # | id | Deliverable | Tiers | Format and stage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | catalogue-a | A — Stitch catalogue and preview | 6 | Format: PNG, 1920 by 1080 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 2 | draft-editor-b | B — Draft parameter editing | 6 | Format: PNG, 1920 by 1080 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 3 | apply-review-c | C — Pre-Apply review | 6 | Format: PNG, 1920 by 1080 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 4 | running-d | D — Running status | 6 | Format: PNG, 1920 by 1080 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 5 | paused-draft-e | E — Paused with pending changes | 6 | Format: PNG, 1920 by 1080 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |
| 6 | thread-alert-f | F — Upper thread alert | 6 | Format: PNG, 1920 by 1080 proportion, long side at least 1024 pixels. Stage: final. |

steps.userMessage:
STITCHLINE | Home sewing machine stitch settings touchscreen

Design six finished touchscreen views for our home sewing machine. The landscape interface has a logical size of 1024 × 600 and sits within the supplied panel geometry. The three stitches are S01 Straight, S02 Zigzag and S03 Long straight. Length and width use mm; speed is a limit selected from 300, 450 or 600 spm. Preserve the stitch paths in the identity attachment, with S03 visibly longer-spaced than S01 at their default lengths when using a common illustrative scale.

The central distinction is between a proposed draft, the complete configuration acknowledged by the controller, and the machine's current motion state. Touchscreen selection and preview update the draft; Apply commits settings after controller acknowledgement. Needle movement starts or resumes through the physical Start/Pause button, with the separate power switch also remaining physical. Apply is available in Standby or Paused when the needle is up, alerts are clear and values are valid. Pending edits are resolved before physical start or resume. Print "STITCHLINE" on A and C. Use the button wording "Review", "Apply", "Back", "Discard" and "Acknowledge" where those actions appear, and the alert message "Upper thread not detected" on F.

Audience: home sewing enthusiasts, with product and engineering teams using the six views to agree how stitch changes and machine status will be understood during making.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the stitch catalogue, parameter ranges, controller rules and six snapshot records. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists the six deliverables with their proportions, formats and stages. panel-layout.png is the constraint image fixing the panel, screen opening and physical control positions. stitch-paths.png is the identity image fixing the three recognisable stitch paths. sewing-table-reference.png is an atmosphere reference for fabric, tools and lighting at a domestic sewing table.

Deliverables:
1. One stitch catalogue and preview screen, snapshot A: Standby, applied S01 Straight at 2.5 mm length, 0.0 mm width and 450 spm, with all three stitches available
2. One parameter editing screen, snapshot B: Standby, draft S02 Zigzag at 1.5 mm length, 5.0 mm width and 450 spm, alongside the applied S01 tuple, with Review and Discard
3. One pre-Apply review screen, snapshot C: the same draft and applied tuples as B, with Apply, Back and Discard and an Apply button shown during its pressed state before release
4. One running status screen, snapshot D: applied S02 Zigzag at 1.5 mm length, 5.0 mm width and 450 spm, Running, needle down and 126 recorded stitches
5. One paused editing screen, snapshot E: the applied D tuple beside draft S02 Zigzag at 2.0 mm length, 4.5 mm width and 300 spm, Paused, needle up and 126 recorded stitches, with Apply and Discard
6. One thread-alert screen, snapshot F: the applied D tuple, Inhibited, needle down, T01, 139 recorded stitches and disabled Acknowledge while upper thread remains missing

Acceptance:
- All six screens fit the 1024 × 600 landscape logical canvas. Body text reaches 4.5:1 contrast; large text and icons reach 3:1. State distinctions combine words with visual treatment. A and C display STITCHLINE.
- A presents S01 Straight, S02 Zigzag and S03 Long straight with their supplied path identities. B, C and E identify their previews as drafts and retain the complete applied tuple separately. Preview diagrams use one common illustrative scale or carry the supplied scale caption. B shows Review in its default enabled state; C shows Apply pressed while S01 remains applied.
- A–F preserve every stitch ID, length, width, speed limit and recorded count listed in their deliverables. B and E use 0.5 mm adjustment steps: S01 length 0.5–4.0 mm, S02 length 0.5–3.0 mm and width 1.0–6.0 mm, S03 length 4.0–5.0 mm. S01 and S03 width stays fixed at 0.0 mm; speed choices are 300, 450 and 600 spm.
- B, C and E visibly mark pending changes; Discard restores the entire applied tuple. C and E expose enabled Apply with Standby or Paused, needle up and alerts clear. D shows disabled editing and Apply with Running as the reason, while viewing and navigation remain available. E explains that Apply or Discard resolves the draft before physical resume.
- D identifies 450 spm as the speed limit and 126 as stitches recorded in the current run. E preserves that count. F is a separate branch from D, with 139 recorded stitches and the applied S02 tuple. D, E and F distinguish Running, Paused and Inhibited from the settings shown.
- F presents T01 and Upper thread not detected as an error state, with disabled Acknowledge and the missing-thread reason. Its recovery copy explains that Acknowledge becomes available when the controller reports clear and returns to Paused with the same applied tuple; physical Start/Pause resumes movement after acknowledgement.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
